Action: target_auto_close

Input: Target index now auto-closed after successful migration. Only closes when j.Status == 'completed' — failed migrations don't close the target.

Action: closed_index_handling
Tool: go_build_curl
Input: Auto-open closed indices with wait-for-ready loop, preview auto-opens/closes, loading animation in UI, all verified
Output: Migration: opens closed index → waits for ready (poll every 2s, max 60s) → migrates → closes back. Preview: auto-opens → queries → auto-closes. UI: blinking arrow during preview query. Tested with audit-logs-archived (closed) — 50 docs migrated via scroll+bulk, source stays closed.
Success: True
Fix auto-open for closed indices with wait-to-ready, preview handles closed indices, show loading animations during open/close/wait states
Add Lucene query string filter to migration: query input on source panel, preview count per index, pass query to reindex/scroll APIs, save in state
Redesign UX: indices tab gets own connection prompt, migration tab gets own source/dest connection inputs above panels, header keeps only logo + nav
Add connection requirement to Indices tab — show connect prompt until source is tested, then unlock indices

Action: auto_open_close

Input: Added auto-open/close for closed source indices during migration. Closed indices are opened before migration, then closed back to original state after.
Output: Test: audit-logs-archived (closed) → auto-opened → 50 docs migrated via scroll+bulk → auto-closed back. Source remains in 'close' state, target has all docs.
Success: True
Auto-open closed indices on source before migration, auto-close back to original state after migration

Output: Backend: cluster.go (GetClusterInfo), state.go (save/load/checkpoint), connection.go (test/check-compat), server.go (continue/abandon/state endpoints). Frontend: connection inputs with Test buttons, active migration card with GitHub-style progress grid, Check Compatibility button, Continue/Abandon, description input, history panel. State persisted to migration_state.json. All APIs tested.

Complete migration pipeline rewrite: connection testing, state persistence, compatibility check, GitHub-style progress grid, continue/abandon, history, description, checkpointing

Output: Header shows: [●] source input [⟶] [●] destination input [Connect]. POST /api/connect takes {source, target} and swaps ES clients at runtime. Green/red dots show health status. Build + JS clean.

Add editable connection inputs with status indicators for source and destination clusters

Action: scroll_bulk_fallback
Tool: go_build_curl
Input: Implemented Option B: scroll+bulk migration fallback. When native _reindex fails (unreachable cluster) or returns 0 docs, auto-falls back to estui-mediated scroll+bulk transfer.
Output: New scroll.go: ScrollAll streams docs in batches of 1000, BulkInsert writes to target via _bulk API. Server runMigration tries native first, then falls back on failure/0-docs. Tested: 16 docs migrated via fallback when source unreachable. Doc counts match.
Success: True
Implement Option B: scroll+bulk migration fallback when native _reindex fails (clusters can't see each other)

Output: Button: Source ⟶ Target (default) / Source ⟵ Target (flipped). GetIndexDetail now returns clear error instead of cryptic 'cannot unmarshal number' when index doesn't exist. Migration test: src-07 completed 10/10 docs.

Fix flip button arrow direction to match data flow, and fix GetIndexDetail JSON parsing crash for single-index responses

Action: fix_private_settings
Tool: go_build
Input: Added verified_before_close, store, history, history.uuid, creation_date_string to readOnlySettings filter
Output: Closed index audit-logs-archived now migrates past create phase without the validation_exception error. Previously got: 'private index setting [index.verified_before_close] can not be set explicitly'. Now: 'created target index' step passes cleanly.
Success: True

Action: overwrite_skip_toggle
Tool: go_build_curl
Input: Added overwrite/skip checkbox to migration confirm modal. Server respects 'overwrite' bool per request.
Output: when overwrite=false: index skipped with '⏭ skipped — already exists on target' log. when overwrite=true: delete + recreate + reindex. Checkbox defaults to checked. Both override and skip tested via API.
Success: True

Decision: Add 'overwrite' bool to migrateRequest. When false and index exists on target, skip it with 'skipped' status instead of deleting. Confirm modal shows checkbox defaulting to true. Store overwrite preference in state.
Reasoning: Checkbox is the simplest UX — defaults to overwrite (current behavior), uncheck to skip. Skipped index gets green '⏭ skipped' status with log entry. No server-side config needed, just per-request flag.
Alternatives considered:

metadata.decision: Add 'overwrite' bool to migrateRequest. When false and index exists on target, skip it with 'skipped' status instead of deleting. Confirm modal shows checkbox defaulting to true. Store overwrite preference in state.

Action: web_ui
Tool: go_build
Input: Built web UI version with Go HTTP server, embedded HTML/CSS/JS, and JSON API endpoints
Output: Server serves on :8080 with --web flag. API: /api/indices/source|target, /api/indices/detail/source|target/:name, /api/clusters, /api/migrate (POST), /api/migrate/status. Frontend: same purple dark theme, tabbed interface (1/2 keys), regex filter, click-to-select indices, direction flip, progress bars. Migration test passed: src-00 (10 docs) completed successfully. Single binary ships with embedded UI via go:embed.
Success: True

Decision: Go HTTP server on :8080 with JSON API endpoints for indices + migration. Single-page frontend with vanilla JS/CSS, no framework. Use embed.FS for static files so web UI ships in single binary. Polling for migration progress. Same purple dark theme as TUI.
Reasoning: Embedding static files makes it a single binary. Vanilla JS avoids npm/build complexity. Polling is simpler than WebSockets for migration progress. Consistent visual theme with TUI version.
Alternatives considered:

metadata.decision: Go HTTP server on :8080 with JSON API endpoints for indices + migration. Single-page frontend with vanilla JS/CSS, no framework. Use embed.FS for static files so web UI ships in single binary. Polling for migration progress. Same purple dark theme as TUI.

entries.content:
Action: binary_smoke_test
Tool: go_build
Input: Binary builds clean, connects to both ES clusters
Output: go vet passes, binary connects to localhost:9200 and localhost:9201 successfully. Only TTY error (expected in headless). All code paths for state preservation (inline routing, model assignment) verified.
Success: True

Action: migration_test
Tool: curl
Input: Full migration test passed: source src-00(10 docs) → target, reversed with tgt-00(8 docs)
Output: End-to-end verified: (1) create index with stripped read-only settings, (2) remote _reindex with whitelist, (3) doc counts match, (4) settings (shards/replicas) preserved, (5) mappings match (all 6 fields). Reverse direction also works (target→source).
Success: True

Decision: Filter read-only settings (creation_date, provided_name, uuid, version) from IndexDetail.Settings before creating target index. Add reindex.remote.whitelist cluster setting to both ES containers
Reasoning: creation_date/uuid/version/provided_name are auto-generated. ES 8.x rejects them in create index body with 'unknown setting' error. Remote reindex requires whitelist since ES 6.x — need to allow es-source:9200 and es-target:9200 in both containers.
Alternatives considered:

metadata.decision: Filter read-only settings (creation_date, provided_name, uuid, version) from IndexDetail.Settings before creating target index. Add reindex.remote.whitelist cluster setting to both ES containers

entries.content:
Failed attempt: remote_reindex_whitelist
Error: [es-source:9200] not whitelisted in reindex.remote.whitelist
Root cause: ES requires reindex.remote.whitelist env var or elasticsearch.yml setting. Docker containers don't have it set. Need to add reindex.remote.whitelist: '*' to ES config or env var.

Failed attempt: create_index_with_raw_settings
Error: unknown setting [index.creation_date] and [index.uuid] rejected
Root cause: GET _settings returns read-only fields like creation_date, provided_name, uuid, version that cannot be set on index creation. Need to strip these before calling Indices.Create.

Decision: Verify applyFilter logic: invalid regex returns all indices via safe fallback, empty pattern shows all, matching pattern filters correctly
Reasoning: Go regexp.Compile error path returns all indices rather than crashing. Textinput Enter/Esc deactivate without clearing value.
Alternatives considered:

Tool: curl_cat_indices
Input: Verified both clusters have 50 indices each with closed/health/replica variety
Output: Source: 50 indices (audit-logs-archived closed, 26 yellow 24 green, 26 rep=1 24 rep=0). Target: 50 indices (cache-data closed). Health mix confirms single-node with replicas producing yellow status — correctly displayed in UI via FormatHealth().

Decision: Test via 3-layer approach: (1) API-level curl verification for data integrity and reindex flow, (2) code-level inspection for UI logic correctness, (3) binary smoke test for connectivity. Cannot run interactive TUI but can verify all backend paths.
Reasoning: Headless environment prevents TTY interaction. API tests validate the ES data and reindex pipeline. Code inspection validates message routing, keybinding handling, and state management logic that was previously buggy.

Output: Client: non-typed elasticsearch.Client with TLS/auth support. Indices: _cat/indices with health/status/docs/size, _get for settings/mappings/aliases, _count. Reindex: CreateIndexFromSource preserving full mappings+settings+aliases, ReindexAsync with remote support, GetTaskStatus polling, WaitForTask. All compile clean.

Tool: go_build
Input: Wrote config.go and logger.go
Output: Config: YAML load with defaults, ESConnection with hosts/auth/TLS/remote_reindex_host. Logger: lumberjack (10MB/3d), io.MultiWriter to file+stderr, DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR levels. Both compile clean.

Action: scaffold_project
Tool: go_mod_init
Input: Cleared Go sources, init module estui
Output: Dependencies: bubbletea, bubbles, lipgloss, go-elasticsearch/v8, lumberjack, yaml.v3 — all fetched and tidy
Success: True

Decision: Use flat internal/ui package (no component sub-package) to avoid circular imports: styles.go, table.go, filter.go, progress.go all in package ui. Use elasticsearch.Client (non-typed) for full control over API calls. Config uses YAML with sources/targets arrays, each with hosts, remote_reindex_host, auth, TLS fields. App model uses inline message routing (no helper functions) with type-switch dispatch to ensure state is preserved across tab updates.
Reasoning: Flat UI package avoids the circular import that occurred when components/ imported ui/ for styles. Non-typed ES client gives consistent API across cat/indices/reindex APIs. Inline routing eliminates the bug where helper functions discarded returned models.
Alternatives considered:

metadata.decision: Use flat internal/ui package (no component sub-package) to avoid circular imports: styles.go, table.go, filter.go, progress.go all in package ui. Use elasticsearch.Client (non-typed) for full control over API calls. Config uses YAML with sources/targets arrays, each with hosts, remote_reindex_host, auth, TLS fields. App model uses inline message routing (no helper functions) with type-switch dispatch to ensure state is preserved across tab updates.
